title: Back-foot bounce and spin
setup: In a 10×8m area, stand 5m from the coach with a cone behind you. Bounce the coach's pass back first time, spin around the cone and receive the return on the move. Pass through a 2m gate to finish.
points: Check before the spin; separate from the marker; cushion the return.
progression: Easier: walking spin and two touches. Harder: coach changes the return angle.

title: Sole stop and reverse release
setup: Place a stop line 6m from the coach and a target gate 4m behind the player. Dribble to the line, stop with the sole, roll across the body and reverse-pass through the gate without turning fully.
points: Balance over the standing leg; scan the gate; disguise the release.
progression: Easier: turn to see the target. Harder: narrow the gate and alternate feet.

title: Touch away from the arriving coach
setup: Use a 10m square. Coach passes from one corner and follows on a diagonal at walking pressure. Player's first touch must move away from that approach, then return the pass from outside the coach's line.
points: Read the approach rather than guessing; keep the ball playable.
progression: Easier: announce the approach. Harder: increase pressure after a clean reception.

title: Receive on a curved run
setup: Set three markers on a semicircle 5m from the coach. Start behind the outer marker, curve towards the middle, receive along the run and pass back before reaching the last marker. Repeat in reverse.
points: Arrive as the ball arrives; show the receiving foot; avoid stopping.
progression: Easier: slow service. Harder: serve to either side of the run.

title: Dead-ball escape from the touchline
setup: Mark a 12×6m strip. Start with a stationary ball beside the touchline and the coach 3m infield. Use a pull-back or outside touch to create an infield passing lane and play through a central gate.
points: Protect the exit touch; use the boundary as information.
progression: Easier: coach stays still. Harder: coach blocks one lane without tackling.

title: Bounce-pass weight ladder
setup: Place three receiving boxes 4m, 7m and 10m away. Player passes to coach in the nearest box; coach returns and retreats to the next. Adjust weight to reach the coach within each box, then work back.
points: Firm ankle; match force to distance; follow through towards target.
progression: Easier: wider boxes. Harder: coach receives moving across each box.

title: Outside-foot pass around a screen
setup: Set a cone screen 2m wide between player and coach, 8m apart. From a ball beside the screen's edge, curve an outside-foot ground pass around it to the coach, who returns down the open side.
points: Contact the outside of the ball; balanced plant; prioritise control.
progression: Easier: smaller screen. Harder: move the ball before releasing.

title: Disguised reverse pass
setup: Coach stands 6m away behind a pair of gates. Player carries across the face of the gates, looks towards one and passes back across her direction into the other for coach to collect.
points: Sell direction with posture; keep eyes aware of the real target.
progression: Easier: stop before passing. Harder: coach signals the available gate later.

title: Driven ground pass through a window
setup: Set a 1.5m gate halfway along a 14m passing lane. Player and coach exchange firm ground passes through it, keeping the ball below ankle height. Move the gate off-centre after each short set.
points: Strike through the ball's centre; stable ankle; receive softly.
progression: Easier: 8m distance. Harder: smaller window, never extra power alone.

title: Lofted pass to a landing square
setup: Mark a clear 4m landing square 10–15m away. Player clips a stationary ball into it; coach retrieves and rolls back. Judge success by first landing inside the square, not maximum distance.
points: Get under the ball; relaxed follow-through; watch the landing.
progression: Easier: larger nearer square. Harder: moving-ball service. No heading.

title: Return pass while retreating
setup: Across a 12m lane, player starts 4m from coach. Coach feeds along the ground while player retreats in controlled steps and returns each ball; stop at the far line, walk back and reset.
points: Stay balanced; adjust feet early; keep hips available to pass.
progression: Easier: pause before each feed. Harder: alternate left/right service.

title: Pass across a moving gate
setup: Coach walks sideways holding the position of an imaginary receiving window between two cones 5m apart. Player, 8m away, times a pass to reach the coach inside the window before she exits.
points: Lead the receiver; look at movement before contact.
progression: Easier: slower movement. Harder: coach reverses direction before the pass.

title: Check away then meet the pass
setup: Set a starting cone and a receiving cone 4m apart. Player first moves away from coach, then checks sharply towards the receiving cone for a pass and returns it. Coach varies when the ball is released.
points: Create separation; call when ready; decelerate before receiving.
progression: Easier: predictable release. Harder: coach delays or changes passing foot.

title: Double-movement pocket reception
setup: Make two 3m receiving pockets 5m apart. Player shows in one, moves out of it, then reappears in the other for a coach pass. Receive facing forward and carry over a finish line.
points: Make the first movement believable; scan during travel.
progression: Easier: pre-agree pocket. Harder: coach shuts one pocket with a step.

title: First-touch distance judgement
setup: Coach serves from 6m into a 12m lane. Before each serve coach stands either near or far beyond the player. Player chooses a close controlling touch when coach is near or a longer running touch when far.
points: Read available space; distinguish control from acceleration.
progression: Easier: clear near/far positions. Harder: reduce the visual difference.

title: Inside hook around a trailing marker
setup: In a 10m channel, carry beyond a cone and hook the ball back with the inside foot before passing to coach at the start. Coach walks behind at an agreed distance to represent a trailing opponent.
points: Lower centre of gravity; turn ball and body together.
progression: Easier: no following coach. Harder: coach narrows the gap without contact.

title: Outside hook into a diagonal lane
setup: Set a central cone with two diagonal exit corridors. Approach straight, take an outside-foot hook and leave through the opposite-side corridor before passing back to coach.
points: Keep the hook close; push the next touch into the exit.
progression: Easier: broad corridors. Harder: coach identifies the open corridor during approach.

title: Drag-back L turn
setup: Create an L-shaped route with 4m legs. Dribble into the corner, drag the ball back under the body and move it sideways with the inside foot to exit along the second leg.
points: Use a stable supporting foot; turn before accelerating.
progression: Easier: separate the two touches. Harder: continuous motion on both feet.

title: Cruyff turn from a crossing shape
setup: Mark a touchline lane and a return gate behind the player. Carry towards the end, shape to cross, pull the ball behind the standing leg and return through the gate. Coach observes the disguise from infield.
points: Make the crossing shape credible; keep the turn within reach.
progression: Easier: stationary start. Harder: coach approaches slowly from the front.

title: Half-turn with a late closed side
setup: Coach feeds towards player between two cones 3m apart, then steps towards one shoulder. Player turns out through the opposite shoulder and returns a pass after clearing the receiving line.
points: Scan as the pass travels; keep both turn options open.
progression: Easier: earlier coach step. Harder: firmer feed and smaller receiving space.

title: Diagonal carry and square release
setup: Mark a 12×10m rectangle. Player dribbles diagonally from one corner while coach moves along the opposite edge. At the middle line, square-pass into coach's path rather than continuing towards her.
points: Carry with head up; separate running and passing direction.
progression: Easier: coach stationary. Harder: coach changes speed along the edge.

title: Tempo-change corridor
setup: Lay a 15m lane with slow, middle and exit sections. Player uses close control in the first section, pauses in the middle to draw coach one step closer, then accelerates through the exit and resets.
points: Change speed deliberately; use a longer touch only into space.
progression: Easier: no coach chase. Harder: coach follows at controlled pressure.

title: Scissors and second-touch exit
setup: Start 5m from a marker in an 8m square. Approach, step around the ball with one foot and exit with the other into a diagonal gate. Coach varies the starting angle each set.
points: Move the body before the ball; commit to the exit.
progression: Easier: walking approach. Harder: coach replaces marker with passive pressure.

title: Body feint without touching the ball
setup: From a rolling coach feed in a 10m lane, let the ball travel, drop a shoulder one way, then take it the other way and pass back. The feint must happen before the first touch.
points: Use eyes, shoulder and hips; delay the touch safely.
progression: Easier: slow roll. Harder: coach closes at walking speed.

title: Stop-start chase window
setup: Player starts 2m ahead of coach in a 12m lane. Dribble, stop the ball once to invite approach, then restart before coach reaches a marked no-contact line. Swap starting gaps after each set.
points: Listen and look; restart with a purposeful first step.
progression: Easier: larger head start. Harder: coach begins closer; no body contact.

title: Lateral sole-roll slalom
setup: Place four cones in a line 2m apart. Move sideways along them using sole rolls to move the ball across the body, alternating direction around each cone. Pass to coach at the end.
points: Keep knees soft; maintain balance; stay able to look up.
progression: Easier: wider spacing. Harder: coach calls a pause and reverse.

title: Figure-eight tight control
setup: Set two cones 3m apart. Complete a figure-eight using inside touches around one and outside touches around the other, then pass through the centre to coach. Change foot after each short set.
points: Use different surfaces with intent; turn hips around the ball.
progression: Easier: 4m spacing. Harder: coach shows a direction change at the centre.

title: Retreat dribble to re-attack
setup: In a 12×8m rectangle, player approaches coach, retreats with two controlled touches when coach advances, then attacks a different side. Success is reaching an end line with control, not beating by force.
points: Retreat while seeing the opponent; change the next angle.
progression: Easier: coach only shadows. Harder: coach can intercept after the retreat.

title: Near-foot interception pass
setup: Coach rolls a ball across a 6m receiving line from the side. Player steps across its path and passes first time with the nearer foot to a diagonal gate. Retrieve between sets.
points: Read speed; plant alongside the path; guide rather than stab.
progression: Easier: stop then pass. Harder: vary feed speed and gate angle.

title: Far-foot reach and recover
setup: Player stands between two cones 2m apart. Coach feeds slightly across the body; player adjusts to receive with the far foot, brings balance back underneath and passes through the starting gate.
points: Move feet before reaching; avoid stretching off balance.
progression: Easier: central feeds. Harder: alternate central and wider feeds.

title: Cutback to a trailing target
setup: Player starts on a wide 12m lane, coach waits 5m behind and infield. Carry to an end line, look back and deliver a grounded cutback to coach arriving in a 3m target box.
points: Scan before the line; pull the pass away from goal.
progression: Easier: stationary coach. Harder: coach varies arrival timing.

title: Low cross through a corridor
setup: Set a 2m crossing corridor across a marked 10m box. Player approaches from the wing and drives a low delivery through the corridor; coach collects safely beyond the far side.
points: Adjust approach angle; contact through the middle; check target.
progression: Easier: stationary ball. Harder: approach at match-like speed.

title: Curl around the blocking cone
setup: Set a cone 3m in front of a target and a ball 8–12m away. Player uses controlled inside-foot curl to send the ball around the cone into the target side. Coach returns service.
points: Angle the plant; wrap contact around the ball; control height.
progression: Easier: closer, larger target. Harder: change the ball's starting angle.

title: First-time side-foot placement
setup: Coach serves ground passes square across a 10m finishing area. Player meets each pass and places it into a marked goal corner without a controlling touch. Walk back between repetitions.
points: Arrive balanced; select corner before contact; guide the finish.
progression: Easier: slower feed and larger target. Harder: change service angle.

title: Back-to-goal spin finish
setup: Start with back to an unoccupied goal, 8m out. Coach passes into feet from in front; player pins a cone marker with her movement, rolls the ball across and turns to finish.
points: Check space; use the first touch to set the turn.
progression: Easier: no cone and unlimited touches. Harder: coach names the finishing side late.

title: Run across the goalmouth
setup: Coach rolls from the side while player curves from a near-post cone across the face of a 6m goal. Meet the pass on the ground and finish towards the far corner; alternate sides.
points: Time the run; meet rather than chase the ball.
progression: Easier: wider service window. Harder: coach varies pass pace.

title: Rebound finish from a safe board
setup: Place a stable purpose-made rebound board 5m from an unoccupied goal. Player passes into it from an angle, moves to the rebound and finishes before the ball leaves a marked box.
points: Anticipate rebound angle; shorten final steps; stay balanced.
progression: Easier: control the rebound first. Harder: first-time finish.
equipment: Balls, cones, secured rebound board, goal

title: Penalty placement routine
setup: Use a marked penalty position appropriate to the goal and player. Agree a short personal routine, choose a target and take one controlled shot, then review choice and execution before retrieving.
points: Consistent approach; commit to chosen target; breathe and reset.
progression: Easier: closer target. Harder: smaller target, without extra running.

title: Free-kick over a low obstacle
setup: With a clear goal area, place a low foam obstacle 3m ahead of the ball. Player lifts a controlled strike over it towards a large target 10–15m away. Coach retrieves from outside the strike path.
points: Choose contact and trajectory; land balanced after the strike.
progression: Easier: remove obstacle. Harder: reduce target width.

title: Corner to a landing zone
setup: Place a 4m target square inside a marked penalty area. Player delivers from a corner arc into the square, aiming for landing accuracy. Coach retrieves only after the ball stops; alternate sides.
points: Consistent run-up; choose height; judge the landing.
progression: Easier: shorten distance. Harder: move the zone. No heading.

title: Defensive jockey and delay
setup: In an 8×10m channel, coach dribbles slowly towards an end line while player delays and guides towards a side boundary. End the repetition on crossing the line or a clean interception.
points: Stay side-on; protect the central route; avoid diving in.
progression: Easier: walking attacker. Harder: coach may change pace once.

title: Recovery run to goal-side position
setup: Coach begins with a ball 3m ahead in a 12m channel. Player recovers diagonally into the lane between coach and target before slowing to defend. End after 6–8 seconds and walk back.
points: Recover towards danger; decelerate before engaging.
progression: Easier: coach walks. Harder: vary the starting side.

title: Intercept the square pass
setup: Set two coach ball positions 6m apart and a receiving gate beyond. Coach moves the ball from one position and passes towards the gate; player starts central and cuts across to intercept on the ground.
points: Read body shape; move as the pass is struck.
progression: Easier: announce pass direction. Harder: coach adds a false preparation.

title: Block the shot lane
setup: Coach carries towards a target from 8m away. Player starts 3m ahead of goal, adjusts to stay between ball and target, and blocks only grounded controlled shots with feet; no sliding.
points: Close space under control; body behind the line; protect balance.
progression: Easier: fixed shot side. Harder: coach shifts ball before striking.

title: Front-foot poke and exit
setup: Coach stands with the ball just outside her feet in a 6m square. Player approaches, waits for an exposed touch, pokes the ball cleanly away and dribbles over an exit line. Use agreed low pressure.
points: Watch the ball; tackle only when reachable; recover possession.
progression: Easier: coach stops ball exposed. Harder: small controlled touches.

title: Track the runner without watching only the ball
setup: Coach walks an arcing run along a 10m line carrying a ball. Player stays goal-side with enough distance to see both coach and a central target marker. Coach occasionally drops ball and plays a ground pass for interception.
points: Check runner and space; adjust sideways; communicate position.
progression: Easier: slow predictable path. Harder: vary the run.

title: Touchline throw-in to feet
setup: Coach stands in a 3m receiving box 6–10m away. Player takes a legal throw-in from behind a marked line, aiming at coach's feet, then steps onto the pitch for a return pass.
points: Both feet grounded at release; ball behind and over head; follow play.
progression: Easier: closer receiver. Harder: receiver moves across the box.

title: Throw-in return under a press
setup: Player throws to coach 5m away, moves infield to receive a return and carries through a gate. After returning the ball coach walks towards one side to represent pressure.
points: Move immediately after release; receive facing the open space.
progression: Easier: no pressure step. Harder: later return and smaller gate.

title: Chest cushion from a gentle toss
setup: Coach gently tosses from 3m to the player's upper chest. Player softens the chest contact to drop the ball into a 2m square, controls it and passes back. No heading.
points: Feet stable; relax on contact; get ready for the next touch.
progression: Easier: lower softer toss. Harder: small side step before control.

title: Thigh control into a ground pass
setup: Coach gently tosses from 3m towards the thigh. Player lifts thigh to cushion the ball, lets it fall inside a 2m box and passes back after one settling touch. Alternate legs.
points: Meet then lower the thigh; maintain balance; watch the drop.
progression: Easier: self-drop first. Harder: pass with the other foot.

title: Individual passing golf
setup: Lay five numbered gates around a 20×15m area with different approach angles. Player passes through each gate to coach, then moves to the next tee with the returned ball. Complete a route, review pass choice and try a second route with player-selected targets. Run three 8-minute exploration blocks, each including brief resets and recovery; allow 6 minutes overall for explanation, water and review. This is not continuous high-intensity work.
points: Plan the route; choose weight and surface; accept a reset rather than force a pass.
progression: Easier: wider nearer gates. Harder: angle restrictions chosen by the player.

title: Wing decision workshop
setup: Build a 15×12m wing with an end-line crossing gate, an infield carry gate and a cutback target. Coach alternates between serving and acting as a controlled defender. Player chooses the available route, explains the cue during rests and repeats with a different coach position. Run three 8-minute exploration blocks, each including brief resets and recovery; allow 6 minutes overall for explanation, water and review. This is not continuous high-intensity work.
points: Recognise defender position; keep crossing and carrying options open.
progression: Easier: coach states the open route. Harder: live walking pressure.

title: Midfield pocket investigation
setup: Create three receiving pockets in a 15m square. Coach serves from different edges and closes one pocket by stepping into it. Player moves to receive in another, turns or bounces back, then offers a new angle. Between blocks discuss which movement made receiving easier. Run three 8-minute exploration blocks, each including brief resets and recovery; allow 6 minutes overall for explanation, water and review. This is not continuous high-intensity work.
points: Scan twice; move out of a cover shadow; allow a bounce pass.
progression: Easier: stationary server. Harder: later closure and reduced space.

title: Finishing choice laboratory
setup: Set three starts: central through-ball, angled carry and side-on ground service. Player chooses an intended finishing solution before each start; coach varies the feed and player may revise the choice. Record what worked during rests, then revisit the least comfortable start. Run three 8-minute exploration blocks, each including brief resets and recovery; allow 6 minutes overall for explanation, water and review. This is not continuous high-intensity work.
points: Match finish to service; use balance and placement; reflect without ranking.
progression: Easier: predictable service. Harder: late target choice.

title: Protect and escape challenge map
setup: Mark a 12m square with a safe island and three exit corridors. Coach applies agreed light pressure; player may protect, retreat into the island once, or turn into an exit. After each short duel reset and discuss the moment an exit became available. Run three 8-minute exploration blocks, each including brief resets and recovery; allow 6 minutes overall for explanation, water and review. This is not continuous high-intensity work.
points: Protect without holding; recognise when to turn; choose safe support.
progression: Easier: coach shadows. Harder: remove island use after successful rounds.

title: Personal movement puzzle
setup: Player designs a route through six markers in a 15m square combining a turn, a pass to coach and a controlled change of pace. Coach follows the route as a moving obstacle at low intensity. Test, explain and redesign the route between blocks. Run three 8-minute exploration blocks, each including brief resets and recovery; allow 6 minutes overall for explanation, water and review. This is not continuous high-intensity work.
points: Link actions purposefully; look up; allow the player to change the solution.
progression: Easier: fewer markers. Harder: coach closes one connection.

title: Defender's delay mission
setup: Set a 15×10m channel with two narrow target gates. Coach attacks one gate; player tries to delay, guide outside and regain without sliding. Swap starting locations each block and agree a personal cue to try; success includes slowing the attack. Run three 8-minute exploration blocks, each including brief resets and recovery; allow 6 minutes overall for explanation, water and review. This is not continuous high-intensity work.
points: Protect the most dangerous route; control approach speed; choose tackling moments.
progression: Easier: walking attacks. Harder: variable direction and pace.

title: Set-piece delivery studio
setup: Use a corner start, a wide free-kick start and a short passing start feeding marked landing targets. Player chooses two deliveries to improve, compares setup and adjusts approach with coach. Use short sets, retrieval walks and target reflection; all receiving is on the ground. Run three 8-minute exploration blocks, each including brief resets and recovery; allow 6 minutes overall for explanation, water and review. This is not continuous high-intensity work.
points: Repeat the preparation; judge delivery by target arrival; explain adjustments.
progression: Easier: shorten distance. Harder: smaller landing zones. No heading.

title: Two-foot connection quest
setup: Set four different ground-pass tasks around a 15×12m space: a short bounce, diagonal gate, moving coach and a longer target. Player chooses a foot at each station, tests a solution and revisits it using the other foot without a timed race. Run three 8-minute exploration blocks, each including brief resets and recovery; allow 6 minutes overall for explanation, water and review. This is not continuous high-intensity work.
points: Explore comfortable contact; adapt footwork; compare solutions rather than feet.
progression: Easier: closer targets. Harder: move before each release.

title: Player-led match moment replay
setup: Player chooses a non-sensitive football moment: a crowded touchline, a turn in midfield or receiving near goal. Mark the relevant space in a 15×12m area. Coach recreates the pass and one opponent's movement. Explore three different responses, discuss and repeat the player's preferred solution. Run three 8-minute exploration blocks, each including brief resets and recovery; allow 6 minutes overall for explanation, water and review. This is not continuous high-intensity work.
points: Ask what the player saw; preserve more than one useful answer.
progression: Easier: freeze the opponent. Harder: vary the coach's response.

title: Two-ball passing square
setup: In a 10m square, one player at each corner, start two balls on opposite corners. Pass clockwise, receive before releasing and keep both balls separated. Reverse direction after a short set. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Check both balls; communicate; weight passes for the next action.
progression: Easier: one ball. Harder: change direction on a named call.

title: Third-player wall combination
setup: Arrange a 12m triangle. A passes to B, B sets back to A, A plays to C moving beyond B. Rotate all roles after each sequence and mirror the direction. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Set at a useful angle; time the third run; avoid standing on one line.
progression: Easier: walk the sequence. Harder: add a fourth passive screen.

title: Split-pair interception
setup: In a 12×8m rectangle, two passers on opposite ends try to pass through two moving interceptors in the middle. Interceptors stay 2m apart. Change pairs every 60 seconds. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Pass when the gap opens; defenders move as a pair.
progression: Easier: wider area. Harder: passers must move along their end line.

title: 3v1 exit rondo
setup: Use a 10m square with an exit gate on one side. Three keep possession against one; after three connected passes, a receiver can dribble out through the gate. Rotate defender every minute. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Keep passing lanes; recognise the exit; defender blocks ball and exit.
progression: Easier: larger square. Harder: require a different receiver for the exit.

title: 4v2 split-line rondo
setup: Mark a 12×10m rectangle. Four outside players keep possession against two inside, earning a point for a ground pass between defenders. Swap defenders every minute, regardless of outcome. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Draw pressure before splitting; defenders communicate gaps.
progression: Easier: more space. Harder: outside players adjust positions after passing.

title: Two-zone transfer
setup: Make two adjacent 10m squares. Three attackers and one defender start in one square; two teammates wait in the other. Connect three passes then transfer; two attackers follow while defender rotates with a waiting player. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Support the transfer; prepare the far receiver; travel after release.
progression: Easier: unopposed transfer. Harder: defender may intercept the crossing pass.

title: End-player bounce support
setup: In a 15×10m area play 2v2 with a neutral end player moving along one end. Attackers combine with the neutral, then carry over the opposite line. Change neutral every 90 seconds. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Use the bounce to face forward; move off the defender.
progression: Easier: neutral has protected space. Harder: defender can track the return.

title: Pass-and-follow crossing routes
setup: Set two diagonal passing lanes in a 12m square. A ball travels along each diagonal; players follow their pass to the opposite end. Coordinate releases so balls cross the centre at different times. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Scan for the other ball; delay rather than collide.
progression: Easier: one ball. Harder: alternate ground-pass angles.

title: Receive between two defenders
setup: Two servers stand at either end of a 16×10m space. A receiver moves between two passive defenders to connect one end to the other. Rotate receiver after four successful connections and defenders each minute. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Leave cover shadows; check both shoulders; use a bounce if blocked.
progression: Easier: defenders walk only. Harder: defenders actively intercept.

title: Overlap timing channel
setup: In a 15×10m wing lane, A passes to B and runs around her outside. B carries infield then releases A into a 3m end gate. C serves the next ball; rotate roles after each run. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Delay release until the runner can arrive; keep width.
progression: Easier: no speed demand. Harder: coach stands as an intercepting screen.

title: Underlap through the inside lane
setup: Mark a wide and inside lane across 18×12m. Wide player receives from server while a teammate runs inside her; a passive defender blocks the outside route. Pass into the underlap; rotate all four roles. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Runner stays visible; carrier draws the defender outside.
progression: Easier: defender fixed. Harder: defender chooses which lane to close.

title: Wall pass around a defender
setup: In a 12×8m channel, two attackers face one defender. Carrier may pass to a side support, run beyond the defender and receive the return through an end gate. Reset and rotate after each attack. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Release before pressure arrives; support gives a clean return angle.
progression: Easier: passive defender. Harder: defender may win and counter.

title: 2v1 draw and release
setup: Two attackers start 12m from an end line, defender 5m ahead. Carrier dribbles towards defender and chooses when to release a teammate or continue. Defender scores by carrying back to the start. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Make the defender commit; support stays onside in the practice space.
progression: Easier: wider pitch. Harder: narrower passing window.

title: 3v2 central breakthrough
setup: Three attackers start across a 20×15m area against two defenders protecting two end gates. Attackers choose a central combination or outside carry. Reset when ball exits; rotate defenders every two attacks. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Width stretches the pair; support behind the ball; defenders cover.
progression: Easier: enlarge gates. Harder: begin with a pressured central receiver.

title: 2v2 cover and balance
setup: In a 16×12m pitch, attackers try to dribble across an end line. Defenders nominate first presser and covering partner through communication, changing as the ball moves. Switch attacking roles each two minutes. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Nearest player delays; partner protects the inside route.
progression: Easier: slower restarts. Harder: coach starts with a wide pass.

title: Press from a curved approach
setup: Two passers work across a 12m line while two defenders start 5m away. On a pass, nearest defender curves the press to block return; partner covers a central gate behind. Rotate roles every minute. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Approach under control; block one option; cover the exposed space.
progression: Easier: passers use two touches. Harder: allow them to dribble.

title: Recover after a beaten press
setup: In an 18×12m area play 2v2. One defender begins behind the carrier to simulate a missed press; her teammate delays while she recovers goal-side. Change the starting defender each attack. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Recover towards danger; avoid chasing only the ball.
progression: Easier: head start for recovery. Harder: quicker attacker service.

title: Transition to four corner gates
setup: Play 2v2 inside a 16m square with four 2m corner gates. On winning the ball, identify a free gate to dribble through; the other pair immediately recovers. Restart centrally after each score. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Look outward after regain; partner opens another option.
progression: Easier: wider gates. Harder: cannot use the last scored gate.

title: Counterpress or protect
setup: In a 16×12m pitch, play 2v2 with a neutral support. On a turnover, losing pair decide whether the nearest can press or both must protect their end line. Neutral always supports possession. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Read distance before pressing; communicate the shared decision.
progression: Easier: pause after turnovers. Harder: neutral changes location.

title: Cutback arrival triangle
setup: Wide player carries to a byline in a 16×12m area, second player delays a central run, third provides service then retrieves. Wide player cuts back to the arriving runner for a ground finish. Rotate each attack. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Look before delivery; arrive late rather than wait in the box.
progression: Easier: catch the pass with feet before finishing. Harder: varied service.

title: Far-side ground-cross arrival
setup: Server feeds a wide player in an 18×15m area. Two runners start at different depths; delivery travels low across the area to the far runner, near runner adjusts to leave a safe lane. Rotate after each delivery. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Stagger runs; communicate; avoid crossing paths.
progression: Easier: no finish. Harder: near runner becomes passive defender.

title: Layoff finishing rotation
setup: A passes into B standing 8m from goal; B lays off at an angle for A to finish while C retrieves. Rotate roles every two attempts. Alternate left and right layoffs. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Set into the runner's path; keep the finish controlled.
progression: Easier: control before finishing. Harder: one-touch layoff and finish.

title: Finish then defend the next attacker
setup: Two start queues face an unoccupied goal on a 20×15m pitch. First attacker finishes; then becomes a defender against next attacker from the other queue. Rotate with a retriever; one ball live at a time. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Recover after the shot; attacker recognises recovering defender.
progression: Easier: defender starts further back. Harder: earlier next-ball release.

title: Two-target combination finish
setup: Play 2v2 in a 16×12m area with two mini-goals along the same end. Attackers combine to switch the finishing lane; defenders protect both targets. Switch possession on regain and reset to start. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Move defenders with a pass; support for a change of angle.
progression: Easier: wider targets. Harder: defenders counter into a start gate.

title: Diagonal target-player switch
setup: Four corner players surround one central defender in a 14m square. Connect a side pass then find the opposite diagonal player through the centre if open; otherwise recycle. Rotate central role every minute. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Look across the whole square; don't force the diagonal.
progression: Easier: walking defender. Harder: shrink the central passing window.

title: 3v3 touchline escape
setup: Play 3v3 on an 18×15m pitch with two end lines. Coach restarts near a touchline; possession team must solve the pressure and carry to the far end. No mandatory pass sequence. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Offer a safe backward option; use the width away from pressure.
progression: Easier: defenders start 3m back. Harder: immediate live restart.

title: Screen and intercept
setup: Two attackers pass in a 12×10m area towards an end target gate; two defenders protect it. One defender screens while partner presses, then exchange jobs as ball travels. Rotate pairs each two minutes. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Side-on screen; check partner's position; intercept rather than lunge.
progression: Easier: fixed attackers. Harder: attackers may carry.

title: Defend a grounded cutback
setup: Wide attacker and central receiver face two defenders in a 16×12m box. Start wide near byline; defenders share ball pressure and central cover. Attackers score by passing through a central finish gate. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Don't both chase wide; cover the cutback lane.
progression: Easier: slow service. Harder: allow receiver to change depth.

title: Mark, release and communicate
setup: Three attackers and three defenders share an 18×15m space. Attackers switch lanes on coach's ground service. Defenders may hand over marking with an explicit call while protecting the end line. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: See ball and runner; confirm a handover before releasing.
progression: Easier: walking movements. Harder: let attackers improvise runs.

title: Throw-in triangle escape
setup: Thrower and two teammates work against one defender beside a touchline in 12×10m. Use a legal throw-in to feet, a short bounce or a turn to carry across the opposite line. Rotate roles. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Offer different depths; thrower joins play; no aerial contests.
progression: Easier: passive defender. Harder: defender pressures the return.

title: Short-corner 2v1
setup: Set a corner and a short receiving position 5m away. Two attackers face one defender; combine short to create a ground cross through a target corridor, or dribble along the byline. Reset after the delivery. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Change the angle before crossing; protect the return option.
progression: Easier: defender 4m back. Harder: live defender from release.

title: Kick-off keep-or-go
setup: On a 20×15m pitch play 3v3, starting from a central kick-off. Attackers choose to play forward if available or retain and create width. Score by controlled possession across an end line. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: First look forward, then choose; teammates spread after restart.
progression: Easier: defenders retreat 5m. Harder: allow immediate pressure.

title: Restart through a spare player
setup: In an 18×12m area, two attackers and a neutral restart server face two defenders. Server begins at the back edge; attackers must create a receiving lane and reach the opposite line. Rotate server every minute. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Use the spare player; change height; don't hide behind a marker.
progression: Easier: wider space. Harder: server becomes pressure-sensitive.

title: One-touch escape with safety support
setup: Four outside players surround a defender in a 12m square. Any player under pressure may use one touch to a supporting neighbour; other passes can take two. Rotate defender every minute. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Prepare before receiving; use the safe pass when rushed.
progression: Easier: unlimited touches. Harder: defender changes pressing direction.

title: Diagonal dribble relay with decisions
setup: Two pairs start at opposite corners of a 14m square with one ball each. First pair members carry diagonally, choose a safe side to avoid each other, then pass to partner. Walk back outside the square. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Share space; look before centre; slow down to avoid contact.
progression: Easier: one ball at a time. Harder: coach closes a centre lane.

title: Pass behind the moving screen
setup: Three attackers form a triangle around one walking defender in a 12m square. Receiver moves behind the defender then checks into a passing lane for a ground pass. Rotate defender every minute. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Change line to become visible; pass to movement not a hidden player.
progression: Easier: fixed screen. Harder: active interception.

title: Support after a loose touch
setup: In a 14×10m area play 2v2. Coach starts each attack with a deliberately imperfect but reachable ground pass. Receiving pair recover control and support before attacking an end line. Rotate receiver each start. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: React together; offer a recovery pass; avoid blame.
progression: Easier: gentler imperfect feed. Harder: defenders close sooner.

title: Carry to commit in a 3v1
setup: Three attackers play against one defender in a 15×10m space. Carrier must move towards the defender before choosing pass or carry to an end line. Rotate defender every minute, with breaks. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Commit without running into pressure; support remains visible.
progression: Easier: broad pitch. Harder: reduce defender's starting distance.

title: Switch the pressing leader
setup: Play 3v3 across a 20×15m area. Coach moves the restart ball from one touchline to the other; defending trio identify a new nearest presser and shift cover. Run each attack to an end-line outcome. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Nearest player leads; other two cover depth and inside.
progression: Easier: freeze before restart. Harder: live central switches.

title: Grounded set-piece second ball
setup: Server rolls a wide free-kick into a central 12×10m zone containing two attackers and two defenders. Compete for the ground ball and attack opposite end gates. Rotate server every two restarts. Use short sets with role rotation and recovery within the allocated time.
points: Read the bounce-free service; react to loose possession; cover a teammate.
progression: Easier: clear slow roll. Harder: vary the entry point. No heading.

title: Three-team possession expedition
setup: Use a 22×18m area with three pairs. Two pairs combine against the third. When defending pair regain, the pair responsible for losing it becomes defenders. A controlled pass through any of four scattered gates earns a point; the same gate cannot score twice consecutively. Rotate partnerships between blocks. Allocate 3 minutes to introduction, three 7-minute game blocks (including brief rests and role changes), and two 3-minute water/review breaks. Adapt work-rest to the players.
points: Look beyond the nearest pass; organise quickly after a turnover.
progression: Easier: larger gates. Harder: score only when a teammate receives beyond the gate.

title: End-zone invasion game
setup: On a 24×18m pitch play 3v3 with 3m end zones. Score by passing to a teammate arriving in the far zone; nobody may wait there longer than three seconds. On a regain play towards the other end immediately. Change zone depth between blocks. Allocate 3 minutes to introduction, three 7-minute game blocks (including brief rests and role changes), and two 3-minute water/review breaks. Adapt work-rest to the players.
points: Time the arrival; protect depth; keep support under the ball.
progression: Easier: deeper zones. Harder: receiver must move across the zone before receiving.

title: Find the free-side game
setup: Play 4v4 on a 28×22m pitch with two mini-goals at each end. A team may attack either target, and receives a bonus if it switches target after drawing defenders to one side. Keep normal goals valid so players retain choice. Allocate 3 minutes to introduction, three 7-minute game blocks (including brief rests and role changes), and two 3-minute water/review breaks. Adapt work-rest to the players.
points: Recognise overloaded sides; move the ball before space closes.
progression: Easier: wider pitch. Harder: defenders can counter immediately.

title: Central island connection
setup: Play 3v3 plus one neutral in a 24×18m pitch. Mark a 4m central island occupied by the neutral. Teams score across end lines; connecting through the island gives a bonus, but it can be bypassed. Rotate neutral each block. Allocate 3 minutes to introduction, three 7-minute game blocks (including brief rests and role changes), and two 3-minute water/review breaks. Adapt work-rest to the players.
points: Use the central player when helpful; don't force entry into traffic.
progression: Easier: neutral protected. Harder: one defender may enter the island.

title: Counterattack with a recovery choice
setup: Play 3v3 towards end goals on a 26×20m pitch. After a goal, scoring team retrieves that ball while coach serves a new ball to the other team. Players decide whether to delay or retreat when temporarily outnumbered. One ball live at a time. Allocate 3 minutes to introduction, three 7-minute game blocks (including brief rests and role changes), and two 3-minute water/review breaks. Adapt work-rest to the players.
points: React to the restart; use numerical advantage; recover centrally.
progression: Easier: serve only after defenders reset. Harder: change restart location.

title: Build through the thirds
setup: Divide a 30×20m pitch into thirds, play 4v4 and allow free movement. Award a bonus when possession travels through all three thirds without forcing a straight-line pass. Normal goals remain available. Between blocks discuss when skipping a third is sensible. Allocate 3 minutes to introduction, three 7-minute game blocks (including brief rests and role changes), and two 3-minute water/review breaks. Adapt work-rest to the players.
points: Move between lines; keep a backward option; find forward-facing receivers.
progression: Easier: extra room. Harder: opponents press from different starts.

title: Rotating neutral touchlines
setup: On a 22×16m pitch play 2v2 with two neutral players supporting along opposite touchlines. Score in end gates. After a pass to a neutral, passer and neutral may swap roles without stopping play. Ensure both teams practise with the neutrals. Allocate 3 minutes to introduction, three 7-minute game blocks (including brief rests and role changes), and two 3-minute water/review breaks. Adapt work-rest to the players.
points: Recognise role changes; offer an inside return; communicate swaps.
progression: Easier: keep neutrals fixed. Harder: neutrals have two touches.

title: Protect the lead scenario
setup: Play 3v3 on a 24×18m pitch with end goals. Each block begins with one team notionally leading by a goal. Leading team chooses sensible possession and counterattack opportunities; trailing team decides how to press. Swap the scenario and review decisions, not just score. Allocate 3 minutes to introduction, three 7-minute game blocks (including brief rests and role changes), and two 3-minute water/review breaks. Adapt work-rest to the players.
points: Manage risk; maintain support; attack when the chance is real.
progression: Easier: neutral restarts. Harder: begin from a pressured defensive restart.

title: Chasing an equaliser
setup: Play 4v4 on a 28×20m pitch. One side begins behind and may send an extra runner forward, while the other side can exploit the space left behind. Use a coach call to reset the scenario in each block; both teams experience both roles. Allocate 3 minutes to introduction, three 7-minute game blocks (including brief rests and role changes), and two 3-minute water/review breaks. Adapt work-rest to the players.
points: Balance attacking ambition with cover; track runs beyond the ball.
progression: Easier: larger pitch. Harder: vary the starting deficit.

title: Corner-to-counter decision game
setup: Play 3v3 on a 24×18m pitch. Every restart begins as a short corner for alternating teams. All deliveries stay on the ground. Attacking side chooses short combination or direct ground pass; defending side can counter into two gates at the far end. Allocate 3 minutes to introduction, three 7-minute game blocks (including brief rests and role changes), and two 3-minute water/review breaks. Adapt work-rest to the players.
points: Keep cover while attacking; defend the next action after clearance.
progression: Easier: defender starts back. Harder: varied corner side.
equipment: Balls, cones, bibs, goal, two gates

title: Throw-in territory game
setup: Play 3v3 in a 24×18m area with end lines. Coach introduces balls only through legal throw-ins, alternating touchlines. A successful retained throw earns territory but teams still need to carry across the far end to score. Let players create their own receiving patterns. Allocate 3 minutes to introduction, three 7-minute game blocks (including brief rests and role changes), and two 3-minute water/review breaks. Adapt work-rest to the players.
points: Offer short and longer options; support the second pass.
progression: Easier: defenders give 3m space. Harder: immediate live marking.

title: Pass, carry or reset mission
setup: Play 2v2 plus a neutral in an 18m square with three scoring gates. Players choose whether to pass through a gate, carry through it or recycle when blocked. Each team aims to use all three solutions during a block, without a fixed order. Allocate 3 minutes to introduction, three 7-minute game blocks (including brief rests and role changes), and two 3-minute water/review breaks. Adapt work-rest to the players.
points: Explain the cue for each choice; keep possession when routes close.
progression: Easier: larger gates. Harder: neutral restricted to two touches.

title: Two-pitch problem exchange
setup: Set two 16×12m pitches with 2v2 games, one using dribble end lines and one using passing gates. Pairs exchange pitches between blocks and discuss how the target changes their support and defending. Keep both games live with short local restarts. Allocate 3 minutes to introduction, three 7-minute game blocks (including brief rests and role changes), and two 3-minute water/review breaks. Adapt work-rest to the players.
points: Adapt decisions to the target; transfer learning between games.
progression: Easier: increase both areas. Harder: pairs propose one new condition.

title: Player-designed rules lab
setup: Start a normal 3v3 game on a 24×18m pitch. During each break, one team chooses a single condition intended to help today's focus, such as a bonus for a return pass or late run. Try it, discuss the effect and retain or change it together. Allocate 3 minutes to introduction, three 7-minute game blocks (including brief rests and role changes), and two 3-minute water/review breaks. Adapt work-rest to the players.
points: Observe what the rule encourages; include everyone's voice.
progression: Easier: coach offers two rule options. Harder: players justify their own.

title: Rescue the isolated teammate
setup: Play 3v3 plus one neutral on a 24×18m pitch. Coach starts each round by feeding a wide player with a defender nearby. Teammates choose support underneath, inside or beyond. Continue freely to goal after escaping; change the isolated starter often. Allocate 3 minutes to introduction, three 7-minute game blocks (including brief rests and role changes), and two 3-minute water/review breaks. Adapt work-rest to the players.
points: Arrive at different angles; don't crowd the carrier.
progression: Easier: delayed pressure. Harder: alternate the initial pressured side.

title: Break the compact block
setup: Three attackers plus a neutral play against three defenders in a 26×20m area. Defenders begin in a compact central shape protecting a goal; attackers may use width, a bounce or a carry. If defenders win, counter into two exit gates. Rotate attacking and defending teams. Allocate 3 minutes to introduction, three 7-minute game blocks (including brief rests and role changes), and two 3-minute water/review breaks. Adapt work-rest to the players.
points: Move the block before penetrating; cover behind attacks.
progression: Easier: larger goal. Harder: neutral leaves after the first pass.

title: Play out against a changing press
setup: Three build-up players start on their end line against three pressers on a 26×18m pitch. Coach privately asks pressers to begin narrow or wide each round; build-up side reads the shape and reaches a far end gate. Regains become immediate counterattacks. Allocate 3 minutes to introduction, three 7-minute game blocks (including brief rests and role changes), and two 3-minute water/review breaks. Adapt work-rest to the players.
points: Notice the press; create a free receiver; avoid preplanned solutions.
progression: Easier: pressers start further away. Harder: press changes after first pass.

title: Support the player who drives forward
setup: Play 4v4 on a 28×22m pitch. When a player carries into the attacking half, teammates decide who supports behind and who runs beyond. Give a bonus for a chance created with both supporting movements visible; keep ordinary goals valid. Allocate 3 minutes to introduction, three 7-minute game blocks (including brief rests and role changes), and two 3-minute water/review breaks. Adapt work-rest to the players.
points: Complement the carrier; avoid everyone running ahead.
progression: Easier: wider space. Harder: defending side starts with a spare cover player.

title: Regain and settle
setup: Play 3v3 on a 24×18m pitch. After regaining, teams may attack immediately or connect a safe settling pass first. Award equal recognition for a justified choice, then play on towards end goals. During breaks compare moments when each route helped. Allocate 3 minutes to introduction, three 7-minute game blocks (including brief rests and role changes), and two 3-minute water/review breaks. Adapt work-rest to the players.
points: First scan after regain; recognise pressure; support the first touch.
progression: Easier: pause on a regain. Harder: smaller area.

title: Street-football problem tournament
setup: Three pairs rotate through two-minute 2v2 games on an 18×14m pitch while resting pair observes one coaching focus. Use end gates, then corner targets, then a player-chosen target rule in later blocks. Observers give one specific positive observation before rotating in. Allocate 3 minutes to introduction, three 7-minute game blocks (including brief rests and role changes), and two 3-minute water/review breaks. Adapt work-rest to the players.
points: Experiment; adapt to opponents; give useful peer feedback.
progression: Easier: wider area and gates. Harder: pairs choose a tactical constraint.

title: Scoop along the ground line
setup: Mark a 4m goal line. From 4m, coach rolls centrally; goalkeeper moves behind the ball, lowers into a secure scoop and returns it. Vary the roll slightly left/right once secure. Work in small sets with reset, retrieval and recovery included. For any landing work use a checked soft surface and coach-led technique; reduce repetitions before technique deteriorates.
points: Get body behind ball; bring hands low; secure before standing.
progression: Easier: slower roll. Harder: slightly off-centre roll.

title: Basket catch from a bounce
setup: Coach stands 4m away and gently bounces the ball towards waist height. Goalkeeper adjusts feet to meet the bounce, receives into a secure basket and resets. One ball at a time. Work in small sets with reset, retrieval and recovery included. For any landing work use a checked soft surface and coach-led technique; reduce repetitions before technique deteriorates.
points: Read the bounce; soft hands; secure against the body.
progression: Easier: predictable bounce. Harder: alternate bounce locations.

title: W-shape catch on a straight serve
setup: From 4–5m, coach uses gentle chest-height hand serves to a ready goalkeeper. Catch in front with appropriate hand shape and bring safely into control; return after each catch. Work in small sets with reset, retrieval and recovery included. For any landing work use a checked soft surface and coach-led technique; reduce repetitions before technique deteriorates.
points: See through the hands; cushion contact; balanced feet.
progression: Easier: closer underarm serve. Harder: one side step before service.

title: Collapse save from kneeling preparation
setup: On a checked soft surface, start from a low supported kneel and practise securing a slowly rolled ball just to one side with coach guidance. Progress to a low crouch only when landing is comfortable; alternate sides. Work in small sets with reset, retrieval and recovery included. For any landing work use a checked soft surface and coach-led technique; reduce repetitions before technique deteriorates.
points: Hands lead to the ball; land along side, not elbow; secure gently.
progression: Easier: stationary ball. Harder: low crouch start. Stop if landing hurts.

title: Low step-and-save
setup: From a set crouch, coach rolls towards a cone 1m to either side. Goalkeeper takes a small step to get closer, then makes a low controlled save. Pause and reset fully between services. Work in small sets with reset, retrieval and recovery included. For any landing work use a checked soft surface and coach-led technique; reduce repetitions before technique deteriorates.
points: Step towards the ball; hands together; controlled landing.
progression: Easier: narrower rolls. Harder: slightly wider rolls within safe reach.

title: Parry into a safe channel
setup: Place two wide safe channels outside a 5m goal. Coach serves controlled low shots from 7m, goalkeeper catches when possible or directs an uncatchable ball towards a channel. Coach collects before next serve. Work in small sets with reset, retrieval and recovery included. For any landing work use a checked soft surface and coach-led technique; reduce repetitions before technique deteriorates.
points: Catch when secure; firm hands for parry; avoid pushing centrally.
progression: Easier: hand rolls. Harder: controlled foot service, no power escalation.

title: Secure the second ground ball
setup: Coach rolls one ball for a simple catch. After goalkeeper places it safely aside and resets, coach serves a second ground ball slightly to the side. Keep the second service conditional on readiness. Work in small sets with reset, retrieval and recovery included. For any landing work use a checked soft surface and coach-led technique; reduce repetitions before technique deteriorates.
points: Finish the first action; reset shape; locate the next ball.
progression: Easier: long pause. Harder: change second-ball direction, not rushed diving.

title: Smother a slowing ball
setup: Coach rolls a ball into a clear 6m channel. Goalkeeper advances to collect as it slows, lowers hands and body behind it, then stands and returns. Coach remains still; there is no attacker or collision. Work in small sets with reset, retrieval and recovery included. For any landing work use a checked soft surface and coach-led technique; reduce repetitions before technique deteriorates.
points: Judge pace; shorten final steps; secure before rising.
progression: Easier: stationary ball. Harder: slightly quicker roll.

title: Close-down and stay big
setup: In a 10×6m lane, coach advances slowly with the ball while goalkeeper starts 4m away. Goalkeeper closes some distance, stops balanced and blocks a controlled ground finish from a safe gap. No feet-first slides or contact. Work in small sets with reset, retrieval and recovery included. For any landing work use a checked soft surface and coach-led technique; reduce repetitions before technique deteriorates.
points: Control closing speed; stop before strike; keep a stable shape.
progression: Easier: coach stationary. Harder: one lateral coach touch.

title: Backpedal, turn and collect
setup: Goalkeeper starts 2m in front of her goal line. Coach points behind one shoulder, goalkeeper turns and moves back to collect a gentle ground roll into that side of the goal area. Reset before alternating. Work in small sets with reset, retrieval and recovery included. For any landing work use a checked soft surface and coach-led technique; reduce repetitions before technique deteriorates.
points: Turn to travel rather than long blind backpedalling; find ball early.
progression: Easier: walking movement. Harder: vary the initial facing angle.

title: High-ball take without opposition
setup: Coach gently underarm-tosses above forehead height from 3–4m. Goalkeeper judges the flight, calls, catches at a comfortable high point and lands balanced. Keep jumps small and take full recovery between repetitions. Work in small sets with reset, retrieval and recovery included. For any landing work use a checked soft surface and coach-led technique; reduce repetitions before technique deteriorates.
points: Eyes on flight; hands first; stable landing; no crowded landing area.
progression: Easier: catch without jumping. Harder: one approach step.
equipment: Ball, gloves, clear soft landing area

title: Cross-flight judgement from a hand serve
setup: Coach gently tosses from a wide position 5m away into an empty 4m catch zone. Goalkeeper decides whether she can step forward and catch safely or should hold position; coach retrieves held decisions. Alternate delivery sides. Work in small sets with reset, retrieval and recovery included. For any landing work use a checked soft surface and coach-led technique; reduce repetitions before technique deteriorates.
points: Call early; judge reachable flight; don't chase an unsafe ball.
progression: Easier: central toss. Harder: slightly varied height, no opposition.

title: Roll-out to a moving gate
setup: Coach moves sideways behind a 3m gate 8m away. Goalkeeper collects a stationary ball, steps and rolls along the ground into coach's path. Reset and alternate rolling arm. Work in small sets with reset, retrieval and recovery included. For any landing work use a checked soft surface and coach-led technique; reduce repetitions before technique deteriorates.
points: Low release; step towards target; lead the receiver.
progression: Easier: stationary target. Harder: narrower gate and changing movement.

title: Underarm distribution to a wide target
setup: Set two 3m receiving squares 8m away on diagonals. Coach occupies one; goalkeeper scans, selects the occupied target and uses an underarm throw to arrive on the ground within it. Coach changes target during retrieval. Work in small sets with reset, retrieval and recovery included. For any landing work use a checked soft surface and coach-led technique; reduce repetitions before technique deteriorates.
points: Select before release; controlled arm path; avoid bouncing at the receiver.
progression: Easier: nearer squares. Harder: later target movement.

title: Overarm distribution accuracy
setup: Coach stands in a 4m receiving square 12–18m away. Goalkeeper uses a controlled overarm throw to deliver into the square with a safe bounce; practise a few repetitions, rest and review before repeating. Work in small sets with reset, retrieval and recovery included. For any landing work use a checked soft surface and coach-led technique; reduce repetitions before technique deteriorates.
points: Balanced opposite step; smooth release; accuracy over distance.
progression: Easier: shorter distance. Harder: smaller square without straining.

title: Back-pass control outside pressure
setup: In a 12×10m area, coach passes back along the ground then walks towards one side. Goalkeeper controls with feet and passes through the opposite outlet gate. No hands on intentional coach back-passes. Work in small sets with reset, retrieval and recovery included. For any landing work use a checked soft surface and coach-led technique; reduce repetitions before technique deteriorates.
points: Scan before receiving; first touch away from pressure; calm pass.
progression: Easier: early pressure cue. Harder: later cue and weaker-foot exit.

title: Clearance from a moving back-pass
setup: Coach serves a ground pass from 10m. Goalkeeper takes a settling touch and clears towards a wide 4m target gate beyond the service point, keeping it away from a central danger lane. Use controlled distance. Work in small sets with reset, retrieval and recovery included. For any landing work use a checked soft surface and coach-led technique; reduce repetitions before technique deteriorates.
points: Prepare body angle; choose the safe side; balanced contact.
progression: Easier: stationary ball. Harder: vary feed angle.

title: Near-post footwork after a cutback cue
setup: Coach carries along a byline 5m from goal, then rolls back towards a cone 6m out. Goalkeeper adjusts from near-post protection to the new ground-ball line and collects the roll. Coach does not shoot while goalkeeper is moving blindly. Work in small sets with reset, retrieval and recovery included. For any landing work use a checked soft surface and coach-led technique; reduce repetitions before technique deteriorates.
points: Release the post position as ball moves; small adjustment steps.
progression: Easier: slow predictable cutback. Harder: vary its angle.

title: Save, scan and distribute
setup: Coach serves a gentle catchable ball from 5m then moves behind one of two wide gates. Goalkeeper secures, looks up and rolls to the coach's new gate after choosing a clear lane. Work in small sets with reset, retrieval and recovery included. For any landing work use a checked soft surface and coach-led technique; reduce repetitions before technique deteriorates.
points: Secure before scanning; don't rush distribution; lead the target.
progression: Easier: coach announces gate. Harder: coach changes gate during catch.

title: Penalty-read patience
setup: Coach takes controlled penalty-style shots from a distance appropriate to the goalkeeper and goal. Goalkeeper holds a legal starting position, reads approach and responds to the strike. Coach avoids maximum power; retrieve and recover fully between attempts. Work in small sets with reset, retrieval and recovery included. For any landing work use a checked soft surface and coach-led technique; reduce repetitions before technique deteriorates.
points: Stay patient; set balance; judge actual ball direction rather than guessing.
progression: Easier: announced side and slower shot. Harder: unannounced placement, not extra force.
